definitions: A contract drafted by one party and presented to another party on a "take-it-or-leave-it" basis, with little or no opportunity for negotiation.
A contract of standardized terms, often pre-printed, where the weaker party has no realistic choice but to accept the terms as presented.
examples: Many insurance policies are considered adhesion agreements.
The court scrutinized the adhesion agreement for unconscionable terms.
Consumers often encounter adhesion agreements when signing up for services.
